statusDefinitions.supported: The outcome has an executable implementation and automated end-to-end contract coverage.
statusDefinitions.conditional: The outcome is executable only when named device, artifact, provider, network, or registry prerequisites are satisfied.
statusDefinitions.limited: A narrower local or protocol outcome works, but the broader user expectation is not yet met.
statusDefinitions.blocked: The user outcome is intentionally unavailable and has explicit blockers.

journeys.outcome: Send one text prompt to a compatible browser contributor and receive an answer with an inspectable signed receipt.
prerequisites: A compatible contributor advertises the exact requested model and runtime profile.
The requester and contributor establish a WebRTC DataChannel.
The prompt passes the public-provider policy classes.
limitations: There is no hosted inference fallback.
The default generation contract is a one-shot deterministic response capped at 128 output tokens.
Provider availability and answer quality are not established by protocol correctness alone.

journeys.outcome: Preserve a request when no contributor is available and, after explicit consent, download the model and run it on this browser.
prerequisites: The device qualifies for the selected model's WebGPU requirements.
The pinned model artifacts are reachable and fit browser storage.
The user explicitly chooses Download and run here.
limitations: The first run may require a large model download.

journeys.outcome: Qualify this browser, load one complete model, advertise availability, answer compatible jobs, sign receipts, and stop sharing at any time.
prerequisites: The device qualifies for the selected model.
The model artifacts load through Doppler and browser storage.
The tab remains open and reachable in the selected room.
limitations: Each contributor loads and executes the complete model; model layers and KV state are not distributed across peers.
Keeping a contributor tab available is voluntary and creates no uptime guarantee.

journeys.outcome: Choose a signed, canary-audited, redundant, or adaptive ring policy and inspect whether the required deterministic receipts agree.
prerequisites: Enough compatible contributors are available for the selected policy.
Compared contributors share the required exact model and runtime profile.
limitations: Agreement proves matching signed artifacts, not factual correctness, honest GPU execution, or absence of collusion.
A one-provider policy supplies accountability but no independent comparison.

journeys.outcome: Inspect this browser's saved answers, contribution receipts, room activity, scores, and technical receipt details.
prerequisites: The browser permits localStorage for local records.
Authenticated coordinator access is available for hosted receipt lookup.
limitations: Primary peer-room records are local to the browser and room.
History and network are compatibility aliases for records, not separate products.
There is no account-synchronized cross-device history.

journeys.outcome: Send an explicitly public protein sequence to a selected ESM-2 contributor and receive a receipt-bound pooled embedding.
prerequisites: The user confirms the sequence is public.
A compatible ESM-2 contributor is available or this browser can load ESM-2.
The sequence satisfies the amino-acid and length contract.
limitations: Private or sensitive biological sequences are not accepted.
The product returns an embedding, not biological interpretation or medical advice.

journeys.outcome: Select a promoted adapter pack for an exact base model and receive a receipt binding the pack, approval, acquisition, and inference result.
prerequisites: A promoted public adapter publication matches the exact selected base model.
The contributor can fetch, verify, and load the adapter bytes.
limitations: The adapter lane is hidden when no compatible promoted publication is available.
A published pack proves custody and compatibility, not task quality.

journeys.outcome: Receive signed points and reputation events after the requester accepts a valid receipt or receipt agreement.
prerequisites: A requester accepts the contributor's valid receipt.
The participating peers retain the signed ledger events.
limitations: Peer-room points and reputation are local replicated protocol events, not money.
There is no globally durable, Sybil-resistant reputation network.

journeys.outcome: Receive monetary compensation for accepted browser inference work.
limitations: No payment, pricing, payout, tax, dispute, or settlement system exists.

openWork.summary: Persist every actual-browser release run as an immutable journey artifact instead of recording a checked box.
openWork.acceptance: The release gate writes all releaseEvidence.requiredArtifactFields to a repository-governed or content-addressed artifact and exposes its path from this registry.

openWork.summary: Measure whether a requester can actually find a compatible contributor and reach a receipt.
openWork.acceptance: A retained production report records discovery success, connection success, receipt success, no-provider recovery, and latency separately.

openWork.summary: Evaluate whether enabled text models produce useful visible answers for the prompts the UI suggests.
openWork.acceptance: A versioned prompt set has machine checks and human recognizability or usefulness verdicts bound to model, build, receipt, and output.

openWork.summary: Provide durable, identity-bound records without misrepresenting localStorage as synchronized history.
openWork.acceptance: An authenticated user can recover accepted receipts and reputation events on a second browser with signature and hash verification.

openWork.summary: Track whether any promoted public adapter is presently fetchable and executable.
openWork.acceptance: A retained production artifact binds publication, adapter bytes, exact base model, browser execution, receipt, and current availability.

openWork.summary: Capture deployed expiration and stale-peer cleanup behavior for relay and hosted signaling paths.
openWork.acceptance: A deployed test proves expired adverts and signaling messages stop affecting discovery and assignment.

openWork.summary: Recover the optional hosted diagnostic flow after assignment expiration or a missed reveal.
openWork.acceptance: Hosted diagnostic tests cover registration, assignment claim, commit, reveal, expiration, recovery, and terminal receipt state.

openWork.summary: Move remote discovery and event gossip beyond the optional Reploid room relay.
openWork.acceptance: Two remote browsers discover, connect, accept a receipt, and converge ledger state without any Reploid server relay.

openWork.summary: Define pricing, payout, tax, dispute, abuse, and settlement authority before monetary rewards exist.
openWork.acceptance: Product, legal, security, identity, accounting, and dispute contracts are approved and tested before any paid contribution claim.

constraints: Do not claim trustless, hardware-attested, or guaranteed honest browser execution.
The metadata relay must not carry prompts, outputs, token streams, model payloads, or full receipts.
Each contributor executes a complete model; Poolday does not claim distributed layer, attention, or KV-cache execution.
Local peer-room points are not money.
A journey status may advance only with executable evidence; narrative or a checked TODO item is insufficient.
